passage:
"No! No! I hate it!" Lalremsiami threw the blocks across the room and kicked the wall. Her face was red and her fists were shut.
Deepika, her mother, did not shout back. She sat on the floor a few steps away. "I'm here. I'll stay."
"Go away!" Lalremsiami screamed, then kicked again, then dropped on her tummy and wailed.
Deepika waited, saying nothing more. After a few minutes the crying slowed. Deepika opened her arms and Lalremsiami crawled in.
Later, over milk, Deepika said, "You were so angry when the tower fell. That's a big feeling. What can we do next time?"
"Kick the cushion," Lalremsiami said.

qa.q: What did Lalremsiami do to the blocks when angry?
qa.a: Lalremsiami threw the blocks across the room.

qa.q: What was Deepika feeling while Lalremsiami screamed "Go away!"?
qa.a: Deepika was probably worried but stayed calm and patient. Sitting nearby and not shouting back show a wish to keep the child feeling safe.

qa.q: What did Deepika do later over milk that taught something?
qa.a: Deepika named the feeling, "You were so angry when the tower fell," and asked what they could do next time. Lalremsiami suggested kicking the cushion.

qa.q: What might it have been like for Lalremsiami when Deepika stayed nearby?
qa.a: Lalremsiami probably felt safe enough to let the anger out and then to come back for comfort. Deepika's steady presence made the tantrum less lonely.

grounding: An angry child kicks and screams and needs help to calm, and a calm mother stays nearby and names the feeling later.

passage:
Teacher's note, Monday. Omkar, age five, was building a tall tower when another child bumped the table. Omkar screamed, kicked the leg of the table and hit the floor with both hands. I did not talk. I moved the blocks out of the way, crouched about a metre away and stayed. Omkar screamed for a few minutes, glancing to check whether I was still there.
When the screaming ran out, I said quietly, "Ready for a drink?" Omkar nodded. At the water jug I said, "You were angry that the tower fell. That was a big, cross feeling." Omkar said, "I wanted it to stay." We built a smaller tower together.
Varun, class teacher

qa.q: What did Omkar do when the table was bumped?
qa.a: Omkar screamed, kicked the leg of the table and hit the floor with both hands.

qa.q: What was Varun feeling and thinking while waiting a metre away?
qa.a: Varun stayed calm and patient, knowing talking would not help yet. Moving the blocks aside and staying close shows a wish to keep Omkar safe.

qa.q: What did Varun do that helped Omkar calm down?
qa.a: Varun stayed close without talking, moved the blocks aside and waited. Later Varun named the feeling: "You were angry that the tower fell."

qa.q: What might it have been like for Omkar when Varun stayed nearby without talking?
qa.a: Omkar was angry about the tower and also wanted to know Varun was still close, glancing to check. Having someone nearby made the anger feel less frightening.

grounding: An angry child kicks and screams, and a calm teacher stays nearby and names the feeling after the child calms.
